messages:
Samir: Heads-up — customer acme-retail reported a sharp embeddings throughput drop starting ~02:15 UTC. They say vectors/sec is ~4x lower, latency p95 went from ~60ms to ~280ms, no code change on their side. They attached a sample request + response showing `vector_dim: 1024` expected but some responses show `1536`. Can someone triage?

Liz: Thanks @Samir — can you paste the endpoint name, model variant they were routed to, and a sample request id? Also which region?

Samir: Endpoint: `embed-prod-eu-west1`. Model in logs: `embed-compact-v1-1024` (expected). Sample x-request-id: `req_0a1b2c3d`. Region eu-west. Customer sent a curl reproducer too.

deploy-bot: deploy noticed: published model-catalog mapping at 1795505400 by infra-bot — added variant `embed-large-v2-1536` and removed `embed-compact-quant-v1-1024` from default routing pool.

Liz: Oh, that deploy looks relevant. Did the model-catalog change unpublish the quantized compact variant?

Marco: Looking now. Quick metrics: GPU pool `embeddings-eu-1` shows sustained 92-98% utilization since 02:10 UTC but SM efficiency is down (avg 41%). Queue depth for the runtime increased from median 20 -> 220. Memory copy times up. Snippet from `nvidia-smi dmon` around 02:20:

```
# GPU  SM%  MEM%  ENC%  DEC%  FB%  temp
  0   41    65    0     0    73   68C
```

Marco: Also seeing many small batches hitting the runtime (batch size 1-4) even though client sends larger arrays — suggests routing to a variant with stricter max_batch_size or different batching policy.

Jia: Routing logs (sample):

```
[1795506162] request=req_0a1b2c3d selected_variant=embed-large-v2-1536 reason=variant_in_catalog
[1795506162] fallback_chain: embed-compact-quant-v1-1024(not_found) -> embed-large-v2-1536
```

Jia: TL;DR: model-catalog mapping removed the quantized compact variant from the default set so smart-routing started selecting `embed-large-v2-1536` (higher-dim FP16 model). That explains both the increased GPU work (1536 dims => ~1.5x FLOPs per vector) and the dimension mismatch reported by the customer.

Samir: Customer saw `expected_dim=1024 got=1536` in their downstream indexer which failed a schema check — they flagged it as a breaking change. They also saw billing spike because larger model is priced higher.

Liz: Can we repro locally quickly with their curl? Samir gave this snippet:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-prod-eu-west1","input":["small text"]}'
```

Liz: Running batch of 100 sequences in python to measure vectors/sec:

```python
import requests, time
payload = {"model":"embed-prod-eu-west1","input":["x"]*100}
start=time.time()
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(r.headers.get('x-emb-dim'), len(r.json()['data']))
print('took', time.time()-start)
```

Liz: I ran that against the endpoint and got `x-emb-dim: 1536` and ~150 v/s. On a pinned request to `embed-compact-v1-1024` I get ~580 v/s.

obs-bot: trace created: https://obs.redwood.ai/traces/trace_1795506 req=req_0a1b2c3d. Profiling link: /dashboards/embeddings/embeddings-eu-1?start=1795504800&end=1795512000

Jia: Root cause hypothesis: model-catalog publish removed the quantized compact variant from the routing pool (accidental deletion), so smart router picked a larger FP16 variant. Two consequences: (1) higher per-vector compute -> lower vps & higher GPU util, (2) different vector dimension -> customer schema mismatch.

Marco: Mitigation options: 
- immediate: re-add `embed-compact-quant-v1-1024` to the model-catalog mapping (fast rollback).
- medium: temporarily scale up `embeddings-eu-1` GPU nodes to absorb load while we fix catalog.
- long: add a guard on catalog publishes that verifies variants' dims and warns on removal of quantized defaults.

Liz: I'm going to re-add the variant now and pin a synthetic route for acme-retail to `embed-compact-quant-v1-1024` until they confirm.

Marco: I rolled back the catalog mapping at 1795509000 — mapping now includes `embed-compact-quant-v1-1024` again. Routing logs after rollback:

```
[1795509065] request=req_0a1b2c3d selected_variant=embed-compact-quant-v1-1024 reason=variant_in_catalog
```

Marco: After rollback I see queue depth drop from ~220 -> ~35 and SM efficiency climb to 78%. Vectors/sec for the customer jumped from ~150 -> ~560 (within 3 minutes).

Liz: Confirmed with customer — they see p95 back to ~70ms and no dim mismatch errors now. Customer asked for compensation due to billing spike; flagged to billing.

Samir: I notified the account team and offered a credit for the extra compute hours. They appreciated the fast rollback.

Jia: Action items:
- infra: add publish-time guard that validates variant dims and ensures compact-quant remains in default pool for `embed-prod` (owner: Marco)
- devex: add an alert for sudden change in `x-emb-dim` distribution for an endpoint (owner: Liz)
- eng-runtime: add unit test to ensure routing doesn't pick higher-dim variant when a compact variant exists (owner: Jia)
- support: follow-up PM with customer on billing (owner: Samir)

Marco: I'll open a postmortem and link the catalog diff: https://git.redwood.ai/model-catalog/commit/abcd1234. Planning to add a pre-publish check by EOD.

Liz: Thanks @Marco @Jia. Leaving this thread open until alerts and guard are in. :thumbsup: 

Samir: Customer happy with fix and credit. Closing loop once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
